{{Short description|Romanian architect (1819–1899)}}
[[File:Misu Popp - Stefan Emilian.jpg|thumb|Ștefan Emilian (portrait by [[Mișu Popp]])]]
'''Ștefan Emilian''' (August 8, 1819 &ndash; November 1899) was an [[Imperial Austria]]n-born [[Romania]]n mathematician and architect.

Born in Bonchida, [[Kolozs County]] (now [[Bonțida]], [[Cluj County]]), in the [[Principality of Transylvania (1711–1867)|Principality of Transylvania]], he was given the surname ''Kertész'' as a child, although his birth name was ''Emilian''. He attended high school in [[Sibiu]]. Then, from 1841 to 1845, he studied at the [[Academy of Fine Arts Vienna]], graduating with an architect's degree. Additionally, from 1841 to 1843, he took courses at the [[TU Wien|Vienna Polytechnic Institute]]. Emilian returned home shortly before 1848, in time for the [[Transylvanian Revolution of 1848|Transylvanian Revolution]]. Pursued by the authorities, he sought refuge in [[Wallachia]]. By 1850, he was back in Transylvania, where he taught mathematics at [[Brașov]]'s [[Andrei Șaguna National College (Brașov)|Greek Orthodox High School]]. He remained there until 1858, a period during which he designed the new school building. Additionally, he was the architect for the first paper factory in [[Zărnești]].<ref name="maftei">Ionel Maftei, ''Personalități ieșene'', vol. I, pp. 229–30. Comitetul de cultură și educație socialistă al județului Iași, 1972</ref>

In 1858, he was invited to [[Iași]], the capital of [[Moldavia]], in order to teach drawing and geometry to the upper classes of ''[[Academia Mihăileană]]''. Emilian remained there for two years, until the founding of the [[Alexandru Ioan Cuza University|University of Iași]]. Additionally, he taught at the military officers' school and the technical school of arts and professions. At the new university, he was named full professor of [[descriptive geometry]] and linear perspective, remaining from October 1860 to October 1892, when he had to retire. Meanwhile, he designed the Iași anatomy institute, the [[Lipovan Church, Iași|Lipovan Church]], and the church in [[Ungheni, Iași|Bosia]]. A single published book of his is known: the 1886 ''Curs practic de perspectivă liniară''. Emilian's funeral eulogy was delivered by [[Alexandru Dimitrie Xenopol]].<ref name="maftei"/>

He married [[Cornelia Emilian|Cornelia Ederlly de Medve]].<ref name="IB">Ionela Băluță, "Apariția femeii ca actor social – a doua jumătate a secolului al XIX-lea", in ''Direcții și teme de cercetare în studiile de gen din România'', p. 71. Bucharest: Editura Colegiul Noua Europă, 2003, {{ISBN|978-973-856975-1}}</ref>
